_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (ADR-0239: coverage
past the first stage comes from a selector swept per game).
kind is "input": the selector is the game's own PASS KEY screen, so no RAM
cheat is involved at all - ADR-0239 section 1's first rung, which is also
ADR-0184 section 3's rank 1 ("game code the developers shipped"): the game
writes its own fight variables through its own routine. Every pass key below
is a PUBLISHED value (the per-value _source lines); none is invented.
Why not a RAM selector: the game's fight id $0001 and its two companions
$0002 (fight data bank) and $0003 (offset within the bank) are published
(DataCrystal, Punch-Out:RAM map) and a pinned triple does load the pinned
fight, but the pass keys reach every opponent the rest of this file names,
so the ladder stops at rung 1.
Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
Every value carries a ramCheck, and ADR-0239 section 4 asks for one on a
byte the stage sets rather than on the selector's own address. The two
rungs need different bytes for that reason.
Rung 1 checks $000B. $0001 (the fight id) looks like the obvious byte and is
a trap: it holds the LIVE fight, so it moves on once the fight ends. Measured
on the 120 s sessions of the first run of this sweep
(runs/f1416/punchout/sweep-first-run.log): 0C Super Macho Man read 0A (the
rank-down opponent the game loads after a loss, the World Circuit's Don
Flamenco), 0D Tyson read 0E and 14 King Hippo (Another World) read 1D, while
03 Don Flamenco and 07 Piston Honda happened to still be in their fight. It
read the pass key correctly in the 26-56 s states of runs/f1416/punchout/
verify/, so the byte is right and the instant was wrong. $000B is the byte
the pass-key routine sets from the key it accepted (DataCrystal lists it as
which password/circuit); it reads 01/02/03/04/05, one distinct stable value
per key, and 00 for all nine rung-2 sessions, which never enter the PASS KEY
screen. The expectations are measured, so the check reads "this session took
its own path and stayed on it" - the warp itself is what `new` counts and
what the screenshots in runs/f1416/punchout/probe/ show.
Rung 2 pins $0001/$0002/$0003, and a pin substitutes on the CPU read path,
so the pinned $0001 reads the game's own 00 in the final state - measured,
not assumed (<name>/end.mss in runs/f1416/punchout/pair/, seven runs, the
pin 0001:0B of the Sandman run reading 00). $0002 and $0003 are different:
the game's fight loader stores back the bank and offset it read, so $0002
reads the pinned value (02/05/01/02/03/04/03/03) and $0003 reads 20 for
Don Flamenco (World). That read-back is the check: $0001 reading the game's
own 00 in the same state is what proves the harness did not write memory, so
$0002 = 03 was stored by the game. Both rung-2 checks carry the caveat
ADR-0239 section 4 describes (fixed in #546: it fires on every address the
session pins, so an "input" profile's values[].cheats pins count too, and
it names the pinned byte beside the observed one), because the same state
cannot separate the pin from a byte the game stored after reading it - here
$0001 reading the game's own 00 is what tells the two apart. Read the two
rung-2 rows with that in mind: the check says the game consumed the pin, and
`new` is what says the fight on screen changed.

navigation.label: pass key (the title screen's CONTINUE option)
navigation.source: The game's own PASS KEY screen. Entered from the title menu: Down selects CONTINUE, then the ten digits. The official manual page 6: "Use the top and bottom of the control pad to select either NEW or CONTINUE. If CONTINUE is selected, use the left and right sides of the control pad to select the pass key, then press the A or B button to input the pass key. If the pass key is correct, the game will begin from the boxing circuit corresponding to the pass key." The same routine is in nmikstas/mike-tysons-punch-out-disassembly (PRG_BankDEF.asm LA370-LA406: $D2 masked #$03 = Left/Right increment/decrement the digit at the cursor, A1History/B1History advance it and the tenth input validates), which is also where 135 792 4680 and 106 113 0120 are compared against the A+B+Select buffer. Typing is 47-65 keypresses per key and each script is generated: scripts/stages/punchout/pass-key.py.

_defaultsComment: entry is the route the non-pass-key sessions would take - the 2026-09-24
route, which presses Start through the title to the Minor Circuit and idles
to the bell (scripts/stages/README.md). No value here uses it: every value
above names its own entry script, because a pass key is what selects the
fight. It is kept so the file stays a valid profile for a value added
later, and because the game's first fight - Glass Joe, the Minor Circuit -
is reached by pressing Start at the title menu, which is the same script.
seconds is ADR-0239 section 6's budget. The body is the game's only stage-1
route: a blind combination loop that never reads the opponent's tells, so
it loses. From the bell it lasts about 70 s (Little Mac is counted out),
and the recording after that holds the count-out, the GAME OVER screen and
the pass key the game shows - the same material for every opponent, which
the sweep's new-tile count does not credit twice.
No lives pin rides with a pass key: the entry is input, not a cheat, so
ADR-0239 section 3 does not apply and the game's own GAME OVER stays on
